newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Investment banker says racism hurts Australia.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Investment banker says racism hurts Australia.

text.p: Asian investors are becoming wary of investing large funds in Australia because of anti-immigration remarks by national independent politician Pauline Hanson, a Hong Kong-based investment banker said on Tuesday.

"Asians who are very familiar with this country and who deal with Australia are having second thoughts about investing in Australia," Trevor Rowe, Salomon Brothers Inc chairman and co-chief executive (Asia Pacific), told a Committee for Economic Development of Australia (CEDA) meeting.
"I find remarks by a certain Australian politician are unhelpful to Australia's business prospects in Asia," said Rowe, who was formerly based in Sydney.
He confirmed after his speech that his remarks were aimed at recent speeches by Hanson, who holds the lower house Queensland seat of Oxley which is based on the city of Ipswich, west of Brisbane.
Her comments about the need for fewer Asian immigrants and criticism of aboriginal welfare funding have caused controvery in Australia with the major parties opposing her views.

"Perceptions are important. We need to try harder and show that the White Australia Policy is well and truly dead," Rowe said in his CEDA speech, referring to an early 20th century immigration policy.
Rowe said he was surprised that a lot of Asian investors had reacted so negatively "as a result of the way the media has handled those issues."
"The only way we can be relevant to Asia is to become competitive and become engaged," Rowe said.
